Business goal: Create one durable entity-definition lineage or a new replacement version under an existing lineage.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can create an entity definition with stable keys versioned attributes explicit validation rules and governed form metadata.
Notes / constraints: The request must preserve stable `entityKey` and `attributeKey` semantics. Attributes must include `attributeKind`, `attributeType`, `valueCardinality`, `label`, `description`, `formFacing`, explicit validation rules, and `defaultFormPatternKey` when form-facing. Computed attributes also require `derivationNote` and `sourceAttributeKeys`. Inline options and options-catalog references are allowed for bounded-choice attributes. Defaults remain implicit and must not be copied redundantly into stored records.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may create durable entity-definition lineages and versions.
Authz scope type: exact create over one entity lineage or version
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before create. Feature validation must enforce immutable key rules, bounded type and rule catalogs, version semantics, typed validation-rule arguments, option-source rules, and form-pattern compatibility against `attributeType`, `valueCardinality`, and `attributeKind` when relevant. Client-supplied system-managed fields must be rejected.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Body creates a new lineage or a new version under an existing lineage using stable `entityKey`, lineage metadata, and an ordered attribute aggregate. Each attribute includes stable `attributeKey`, kind, type, cardinality, label, description, optional help text, optional placeholder text, `formFacing`, optional default pattern key, ordered validation rules with typed arguments, optional inline options or options-catalog reference, and computed-attribute metadata when relevant.
Response contract: Returns persisted lineage detail plus created version detail with internal UUIDs stable external keys lifecycle timestamps ordered attributes ordered validation rules ordered inline options and computed-source links. Response separates stored truth from any derived export view.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload including bad normalization unsupported catalog keys malformed typed rule arguments invalid computed dependencies or incompatible form-pattern selection; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 referenced lineage or options catalog not found when applicable; 409 duplicate entityKey duplicate version number duplicate attributeKey within one version or invalid replacement semantics.
Cross-feature seams: Future capability-matrix drafting PRD planning blueprinting and data-dictionary refresh must consume public read or export seams rather than private persistence internals.
Persistence impact: Insert one entity-definition lineage when new plus one immutable version row normalized attribute rows validation-rule rows inline-option rows and computed-source-link rows.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique index on `entityKey`. Unique index on `(entityDefinitionId, versionNumber)`. Partial unique index for one active version per lineage. Unique index on `(entityDefinitionVersionId, attributeKey)` and display order support across attributes rules options and computed-source links. Secondary indexes on status updatedAt attributeType attributeKind and valueCardinality.
Search / filter model: Exact create only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Backwards compatibility is required by default. Stable keys do not change across versions. Replacements happen by new version rows under the same lineage. Historical honesty depends on version-aware catalog resolution rather than copying defaults onto stored rows.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local aggregate validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1. Any later UI must use approved form-template posture and approved child seams only.
Audit requirement: Audit successful creates and denied attempts through the platform's existing audit-visible mechanisms; first-class entityBuilder audit entities remain deferred.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; stores internal planning and field-definition metadata but no direct end-user personal data in the first slice.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and input-validation relevance. Anti-drift rebuild-from-spec and data-governance relevance are high because this becomes upstream repo entity truth.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can create one durable entity-definition lineage or replacement version with stable keys explicit attribute truth explicit validation rules explicit bounded options governed form compatibility and server-owned lifecycle fields.

Business goal: Allow privileged operators to revise a draft entity-definition version before activation or supersession.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can edit draft version content without recreating the whole lineage while keeping stable identity and version semantics honest.
Notes / constraints: `entityKey` and `attributeKey` remain immutable. Updates may revise metadata, attribute details, validation rules, option rows, and computed dependencies only within draft-safe lifecycle rules. Active versions should not silently mutate; replacement should happen through a new version.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may update draft entity-definition versions.
Authz scope type: exact mutation over one draft version
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before update. Feature validation must re-check bounded catalogs typed-rule arguments form-pattern compatibility option rules and computed-source integrity. Successful updates must refresh updatedAt across changed records.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Exact version id param required. Body may update draft-safe lineage metadata and the full ordered attribute aggregate, but must not silently mutate stable external keys or active historical versions.
Response contract: Returns updated stored lineage and version detail with refreshed timestamps ordered attributes rules options and source links. Response must keep persisted truth distinct from any derived effective-view projection.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload or illegal lifecycle mutation; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 version not found; 409 duplicate key collision or attempted mutation of non-draft version.
Cross-feature seams: Downstream consumers rely on stable exported truth so update behavior must keep key churn and active-version mutability non-silent.
Persistence impact: Mutates one draft version and its child rows while preserving lineage identity and stable external keys.
Indexes / uniqueness: Same indexes as create plus lifecycle indexes on active and superseded timestamps. Active-version rows must remain immutable through normal update behavior.
Search / filter model: Exact update only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Backwards compatibility is required by default. Changes to an active definition should land as a replacement version rather than an in-place mutation.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local aggregate validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit successful draft updates and denied attempts through existing platform audit-visible mechanisms.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; stores planning metadata only but can materially affect downstream truth if mutated carelessly.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and integrity relevance. Repo-health relevance is high because silent draft-vs-active confusion would create drift.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can revise a draft version while preserving stable identity bounded catalog validity and non-silent version semantics.

Business goal: Retrieve the current active definition for a stable entity key.
User outcome: A privileged root operator or downstream planner can resolve the effective current definition by `entityKey` without knowing internal version identifiers.
Notes / constraints: This is the everyday lookup seam. It should return the active version under one lineage when present and should remain clearly separated from exact historical lookup and from derived export shapes.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may read stored entity-definition truth in the first slice.
Authz scope type: exact read by stable external key
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before exact read. Feature returns the active version by stable `entityKey` and should exclude archived-only lineages from the normal current-read seam.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Response contract: Returns stored lineage detail plus the active version and its ordered attributes rules options and computed-source links as authoritative persisted truth.
Error contract: 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 lineage or active version not found under normal visibility rules.
Cross-feature seams: Future planners and data-dictionary sync should use this public seam rather than direct table access when they need the current version only.
Persistence impact: Read one lineage and its current active version with child rows. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on `entityKey`, `currentVersionId`, and child foreign keys support exact current reads.
Search / filter model: Exact read only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Current lookup by `entityKey` must remain available alongside exact historical lookup by version id.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local lifecycle visibility rules.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied exact reads if planner visibility is treated as privileged; successful reads optional.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; exposes internal planning metadata only to privileged root operators.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization relevance and anti-drift relevance because this is the normal current-state lookup seam.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can retrieve the current active definition by stable `entityKey` without ambiguity about authoritative versus derived truth.

Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Response contract: Returns stored lineage detail plus the requested version and its ordered attributes rules options and computed-source links as authoritative persisted truth.
Cross-feature seams: Future audit reconstruction and data-dictionary history flows should use this seam instead of re-deriving historical state from current rows only.

Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can retrieve one exact version by durable id for deterministic reconstruction.

Notes / constraints: List response should stay summary-oriented and must not collapse child detail into lossy metadata. Search should operate on normalized `entityKey` and `entityName`. The list may include current-version summary metadata and optional exact-version targeting fields.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability

Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before list read. Feature validation must enforce page pageSize lifecycle filters and sort direction using repo defaults.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Query may include page pageSize optional lifecycle status optional search and optional sort. Defaults follow repo pagination rules.
Response contract: Returns paginated summary rows with lineage id stable `entityKey` entityName currentVersionId currentVersionNumber status updatedAt and export-readiness summary fields when available.
Cross-feature seams: Future planners and generators may use this list seam for entity selection before requesting current or exact reads.
Persistence impact: Read paginated lineage and current-version summary rows. No mutation.

Compatibility / migration notes: Keep list output stable so future planner UI and downstream loops can adopt it without redefining selection behavior.

Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can list entity definitions with stable pagination lifecycle filtering and normalized search.

Cross-feature seams: Entity-definition create update validate and downstream planners should share this catalog seam instead of duplicating design-system assumptions.

Business goal: Tell whether one stored entity-definition version is structurally valid for activation export and downstream consumption.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can see blocking issues before activation export or downstream planning uses the entity-definition version.
Notes / constraints: Validation must remain read-only. It should report blocking issues for missing required attribute truth incompatible form patterns invalid computed dependencies malformed typed rule arguments invalid option posture and lifecycle ineligibility. Effective defaults are resolved through version-aware catalogs during validation rather than copied into stored rows.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may validate stored entity-definition versions in the first slice.
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before validation. Feature should evaluate the stored version against the current version-aware type catalog validation defaults approved form-pattern catalog normalization rules and lifecycle rules and return explicit blocking issues warnings activation eligibility and export eligibility.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Exact version id param required. No body required in v1.
Response contract: Returns validation summary with passFailState blockingIssues warnings activationEligibility and exportEligibility derived from current version-aware server truth.
Error contract: 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 version not found; 409 optional if validation is requested on an ineligible lifecycle state instead of returning a blocking issue payload.
Cross-feature seams: Export and downstream consumers should rely on this validation model rather than re-implementing compatibility and catalog-resolution checks independently.
Persistence impact: Read-only validation over one stored entity-definition version. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on version id and child foreign keys support exact validation reads. Validation itself introduces no new search model.
Search / filter model: Exact validation only; no search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Keep validation side-effect free so downstream loops can trust it as an honest preflight check instead of a mutating repair step.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local validation engine.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied validation attempts if planner surfaces are privileged; successful validation auditing optional.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; validation reveals internal planning issues only to privileged root operators.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and integrity relevance. Anti-drift relevance is high because this protects downstream planning honesty.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator receives honest blocking issues and warnings for activation and export readiness without the feature mutating stored truth.

Business goal: Export deterministic derived entity truth for downstream planning and implementation loops without replacing the persisted source of truth.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can export one or more validated entity-definition versions into a stable derived snapshot shape for downstream capability-matrix drafting and later planning flows.
Notes / constraints: Exported truth is derived and must be clearly marked as such. The canonical snapshot shape should carry an explicit export-format version and preserve stable entity and attribute keys version metadata resolved effective defaults explicit validation rules option truth computed dependencies and approved form-pattern references. Default exports should target active versions only, while superseded or archived versions remain explicitly exportable through historical selection.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may export derived entity truth in the first slice.
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in v1 because the first slice is backend and export focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before export. Feature must validate export eligibility resolve effective defaults through version-aware catalogs and produce deterministic ordering for versions attributes validation rules options and computed-source links. Exports are generated on demand and do not create durable snapshot records in v1.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Request identifies selected active versions by default or explicitly selected exact version ids for historical export. Export scope must be explicit.
Response contract: Returns canonical derived snapshot content or an export artifact reference containing export-format version markers stable keys version metadata resolved effective defaults ordered attributes validation rules option rows computed-source links and governed form metadata while clearly labeling the output as derived truth.
Error contract: 400 invalid export scope; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 selected version not found; 409 export blocked by validation failure or lifecycle ineligibility.
Cross-feature seams: Future capability-matrix drafting PRD planning blueprinting and data-dictionary refresh should consume this explicit export seam rather than reconstructing snapshots from private storage.
Persistence impact: Read selected persisted versions and derive canonical export snapshots on demand. Derived output itself is not authoritative persisted truth and is not stored durably in v1.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on status updatedAt entityDefinitionId entityDefinitionVersionId and current-version references support export selection. Export ordering must be deterministic.
Search / filter model: Export by selected ids or explicit scope only in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Persisted truth and exported truth must stay separate. Later export-shape evolution should use explicit export-format versioning rather than silently changing prior consumer assumptions.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local export eligibility validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit successful exports and denied export attempts through existing platform audit-visible mechanisms.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; exports internal planning metadata for downstream repo use but no direct end-user personal data in the first slice.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and integrity relevance. Standards and repo-health review matter because this seam feeds downstream autonomous loops and future data-dictionary synchronization.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can export deterministic derived entity snapshots from validated stored versions with stable keys explicit export-format versioning resolved defaults and no confusion between derived and durable truth.
